title: Timed Simulator Returns the Answer
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-code scheme and $U$ a finite binary Turing machine. Suppose that for every pair of binary strings $\alpha,x$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes output $w$ on input $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes $1w$ on input $\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ in exactly $S$ steps; and if it computes no output on $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ computes the one-bit string $0$ on that encoded input in exactly $S$ steps, where $S=(3|\alpha|+14T_c(|\alpha|)+50)(t+1)^2$. Then $U$ computes on that encoded input, in exactly $S$ steps, the word that is $1w$ when the decoded machine has halted by time $t$ with output $w$, and is the one-bit string $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $U$ is a finite binary Turing machine
For every $\alpha,x,t$, each output computed by the decoded machine at exactly time $t$ is returned with a leading $1$ by $U$ in exactly the stated $S$ steps
For every $\alpha,x,t$, if the decoded machine computes no output at exactly time $t$, then $U$ returns $0$ in exactly the stated $S$ steps
